st: In a bowl, mix the chicken with the yogurt, [[3 clove]] of the garlic, [[1.5 tsp]] of the ginger, [[1 tsp]] garam masala, the chili powder and a good pinch of salt.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 30 minutes, or up to overnight.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken in batches for about 4 minutes per batch until browned in spots. It does not need to be cooked through yet. Set aside.
In the same pan, melt [[2 tbsp]] of the butter over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the remaining garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes with [[1 tsp]] garam masala and the sugar. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Blend the sauce with an immersion blender or in a regular blender until smooth, then return it to the pan.
Add the chicken and any juices, then simmer gently for 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) inside.
Stir in the cream, the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter and the fenugreek leaves. Heat for 2 minutes without boiling hard.
Taste, add salt as needed, and serve with rice or naan.
Mix the chicken with the yogurt, garlic, ginger, [[2 tsp]] garam masala, turmeric, chili powder, half of the mint and cilantro, and [[2 tsp]] salt. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] ghee in a pan over medium heat and fry the onions for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Set half aside for layering.
Add the marinated chicken and the other half of the onions to the pan and cook for 20 minutes, covered, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil with [[2 tbsp]] salt, the cloves, cinnamon and cardamom.
Add the rice and boil for 5 minutes only, until about 70 percent cooked. Drain well.
Spread half of the rice over the chicken in the pan. Top with half the reserved onions, herbs and the remaining garam masala.
Add the rest of the rice, then the remaining onions and herbs. Drizzle with the saffron milk and the remaining [[2 tbsp]] ghee.
Cover with foil and a tight lid. Cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes so the rice steams.
Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Make sure the chicken reads 165°F (74°C).
Gently fluff from the bottom up and serve with raita.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chili and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coriander, turmeric and chili powder with [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook for 8 minutes, mashing the tomatoes, until the oil separates from the paste.
Add the chickpeas and the water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat.
Simmer partly covered for 15 minutes. Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice. Taste and add salt if needed.
Top with cilantro and serve with rice, naan or bhatura.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted and bright green.
Drain the spinach and plunge it into cold water. Squeeze out the extra water and blend with the green chili into a coarse puree.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Fry the paneer cubes for 4 minutes, turning, until golden on a few sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, heat the remaining [[2 tbsp]] oil. Add the cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then the onion. Cook for 7 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato, coriander and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the spinach puree and stir well. Simmer on low for 6 minutes.
Stir in the cream and garam masala, then add the paneer. Warm gently for 3 minutes.
Taste, adjust salt, and serve with naan or rice.

ing: toor dal or split pigeon peas, rinsed
st: Put the lentils, water, turmeric and half of the tomato in a pot. Bring to a boil, then skim any foam.
Lower the heat, partly cover, and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are very soft.
Mash the lentils lightly with a whisk or spoon. Stir in [[1 tsp]] salt and add a little hot water if too thick.
For the tadka, heat the ghee in a small pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and wait until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and dried chilies and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rest of the tomato and the chili powder. Cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Pour the sizzling mixture over the dal and stir.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro. Serve with rice or roti.
Mix the chicken with [[0.5 cup]] yogurt, half the garlic, half the ginger, [[1 tsp]] garam masala, the paprika, cumin, lemon juice and [[1 tsp]] salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven broiler on high with a rack near the top. Thread chicken on skewers or lay on a lined tray.
Broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and 165°F (74°C) inside.
Meanwhile, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 7 minutes until soft.
Add the remaining garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree, remaining [[1 tsp]] garam masala, the sugar and a pinch of salt. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Stir in the remaining [[0.25 cup]] yogurt off the heat so it does not curdle, then add the cream.
Add the grilled chicken and simmer for 5 minutes. Add a splash of water if too thick.
Top with cilantro and serve with rice or naan.

ing: for the batter, plus more as needed
st: Soak the rice together with the fenugreek seeds in water for 6 hours. Soak the urad dal in a separate bowl for the same time.
Drain and grind the dal with [[0.5 cup]] of the water into a very fluffy batter. Grind the rice with the rest of the water until fine but slightly gritty.
Mix both batters with the [[1.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl, cover loosely, and leave in a warm place for 8 to 10 hours until bubbly and sour-smelling.
For the filling, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan. Add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves, chili and ginger.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Crumble in the potatoes, mix well with a splash of water, and cook for 3 minutes. Keep warm.
Heat a flat nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and wipe with a little oil. Thin the batter with water to the texture of heavy cream.
Pour a ladle of batter in the center and spread outward in a thin circle. Drizzle a little oil around the edge.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Spoon filling onto one half, fold over, and serve with chutney.

ing: for the dough, plus oil for frying
st: Mix the flour with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[4 tbsp]] oil. Add water a little at a time and knead for 5 minutes into a stiff dough. Rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] of the frying oil in a pan. Add the cumin seeds, onion, chili and ginger and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes, peas, coriander, garam masala and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Mix well, cook for 3 minutes, and cool completely.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Roll each into an oval, then cut in half to make 12 half circles.
Take one half circle, brush the straight edge with water, and fold into a cone, overlapping the edges.
Fill the cone with about [[2 tbsp]] of filling, brush the open rim with water, and press firmly to seal.
Heat the frying oil in a deep pot to 325°F (160°C). Fry the samosas in batches over medium-low heat.
Fry for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and serve warm with chutney.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, salt and baking powder in a large bowl. Add the yeast milk, yogurt and oil.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft. Add a spoonful of flour only if it is very sticky.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and cilantro.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into a teardrop about 1/4 inch thick.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Cook one naan for 1 to 2 minutes until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook the second side for 1 to 2 minutes until charred in spots. Brush with garlic butter and keep wrapped in a towel while you cook the rest.
Mix the semolina, flour, baking soda and a pinch of salt. Add the warm water slowly and knead into a stiff dough. Cover with a damp cloth for 20 minutes.
Knead the dough again briefly and roll it very thin. Cut small circles about 1.5 inches wide with a cap or cutter.
Heat the frying oil to 375°F (190°C). Fry the circles a few at a time, pressing gently with a spoon so they puff into hollow balls.
Fry until golden and crisp, about 1 to 2 minutes, then drain on paper towels. Cool fully so they stay crisp.
Blend the mint, cilantro, chilies, ginger, tamarind paste, cumin and black salt with a little cold water into a smooth paste.
Stir the paste into the [[4 cup]] of cold water. Taste and add salt, then chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the potatoes, chickpeas, chaat masala and a pinch of salt for the filling.
To serve, crack a hole in the top of each puri, add a spoonful of filling, pour in the cold spiced water, and eat in one bite.
Boil the sugar, water and cardamom in a pot for 5 minutes until slightly sticky. Stir in the rose water and keep warm.
Mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda in a bowl. Add the ghee and rub it in with your fingers.
Add the warm milk a tablespoon at a time and mix gently into a soft dough. Do not knead hard or the balls will turn tough.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes. Rub a little ghee on your palms and roll into 12 smooth balls with no cracks.
Heat the frying oil over low heat to about 285°F (140°C). It must be gentle.
Fry the balls in small batches for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring the oil around them, until deep golden brown all over.
Drain briefly and drop into the warm syrup right away.
Soak for at least 30 minutes so they swell and absorb syrup. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Peel and dice the mango if you are using fresh fruit.
Put the mango, yogurt, milk and sugar into a blender.
Add the cardamom and the ice cubes.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth.
Taste and add more sugar if the mango is not very sweet.
Pour into two glasses and serve cold right away.
